description: THE single source of truth for character/agent dimensions and every clearance derived from them. Change a body here, re-run the gates, and every validator, bake, and walktest agrees. See AGENT_CONTRACT.md for the derivation rules and what to re-run after a change.

player.chest_note: WHERE A SHOT IS AIMED, and the other half of the geometry that decides how tall cover must be. Derived: the centre of mass of a standing adult sits at about 0.55 of stature, so 0.55 * 1.8 = 0.99, ratified at 1.0. THE HARD CONSTRAINT IS NOT ANTHROPOMETRY THOUGH, it is that the aim point must lie inside the target's own collider -- a line-of-sight ray is cast AT this height and LOS is granted only if it hits the target body first, so an aim point above the capsule misses and every sightline on the map reads blocked. Safe band for a capsule of radius R and height H is R <= chest <= H - R (0.35 to 1.45 here); outside the cylindrical section the ray grazes a hemisphere, and at the apex it misses. A 1.0 m character aimed at a fixed 1.0 m is aimed at the top of its own head.
player.radius_note: BUILD A BODY FROM THIS RADIUS. Not nav_bake.agent_radius_m, which is 0.4 and is a BAKE parameter with 'fattest navigating character + 0.05 safety' already folded into it. The confusion has cost two defects: clearances.unassisted_step_max_m was derived from the bake radius and recorded 0.117 while the gate enforcing it reported 0.103, and Laser Tag's evaluation pill was built at 0.40 so every door-width test ran against a proxy 14% fatter than the character it stood for, spending the safety margin twice (roadmap 123). A body is 0.35; the mesh it walks on is baked for 0.40 so that 0.35 has somewhere to stand.

npc_standard.note: cops/civilians share player metrics until a distinct class ships

nav_bake.note: radius = fattest navigating character + 0.05 safety -- so it is NOT a body radius and nothing should be built at it; see characters.player.radius_note. max_slope sits ABOVE the steepest legal stair pitch (~45 deg; slope legality is validate.py's job, connectivity is the bake's). Voxel erosion is ceil(radius/cell) whole cells per side -- keep cell_size small enough that legal doors survive (see clearances.min_door_width_m derivation).
nav_bake.agent_max_climb_derivation: Was 0.5. The navmesh routes a body over any riser up to this height; a capsule only WALKS up radius * (1 - cos(floor_max_angle)) = 0.117. Everything between was a route the bake promised and the body could not take. Measured on walkup_siege 2026-07-28: the walkers' route crossed a staircase's open lateral edge, a 0.49 m stringer, and four of them parked against it with a horizontal contact normal. Set to exactly one cell_height voxel (0.15) because Godot FLOORS this to whole voxels and warns that it does -- asking for 0.117 at this cell height quantises to zero and disconnects the map. Stairs are unaffected: Deli Counter gives them a smooth ramp collider rather than per-step boxes, so they connect by agent_max_slope, not by climb. The alternative -- enforcing lateral containment on every flight -- was rejected because it would put a barrier along the sides of every staircase in every building; open-sided stairs are ordinary architecture and the bake, not the building, is what was making the false claim.
nav_bake.cell_size_derivation: Was 0.15. Recast joins adjacent voxel columns only within walkableClimb, and on a ramp that gap is cell_size * tan(pitch). So the steepest ramp that stays CONNECTED is atan(agent_max_climb_m / cell_size_m) -- 0.15 with a climb of 0.15 capped that at 45.0 deg while agent_max_slope_deg says 55.0. Measured 2026-07-29: eight path proofs across central_vault and warehouse_district failed as 'disjoint islands', every one of them a storey change, because those buildings have 4.2-5.0 m storeys over a 4.0 m run (46-51 deg) while walkup_siege's 3.2 m storeys (38.7 deg) stayed connected and passed the same sweep. agent_max_climb serves two jobs -- permitting real steps, and permitting the voxel staircase a continuous slope becomes -- and no value of it does both while cell_size is coarse. 0.1 is the largest cell that carries 55.0 deg (56.3 deg), at 2.25x the horizontal columns and so a slower bake. Raising climb instead would re-permit the 0.16 kerb, which is the defect this is protecting.

clearances.derivation: min_door_width_m IS A DESIGN MINIMUM, NOT THE BAKE'S. The bake needs the doorway erosion leaves: min_door_width >= 2*ceil(agent_radius/cell_size)*cell_size + 2*cell_size, which at this contract's nav_bake (radius 0.4, cell 0.1) is 2*4*0.1 + 0.2 = 1.00. It was first worked at a 0.15 m cell -- 2*ceil(0.4/0.15)*0.15 + 0.3 = 1.2, ratified 1.25 for margin -- and when cell_size_m moved to 0.1 (nav_bake.cell_size_derivation) the 1.25 stayed. The walker kept it, 2026-10-13, as the width a walkable door is built to: a 0.35 m body passes it with 0.275 m a side. Deli Counter writes every walkable door it makes at it -- presets.DOOR_W, a width-less door's default (spec_types.Opening.resolved), the staff door behind a teller line (level_design._STAFF_DOOR_WIDTH) -- and builds the island aisle (level_design.island_aisle_width) and the stair landing's opening (stairwell, 0.8 + this) from it, so lowering it toward 1.00 narrows every one of them. What was widened to meet it, and the two doors that are not: min_door_width_note. min_corridor = 2*agent_radius + 0.3 body margin.
clearances.min_door_width_note: THE DOORS WERE WIDENED TO THIS NUMBER; THE NUMBER WAS NOT LOWERED TO THE DOORS (Deli Counter 0.214.0, factory roadmap 197). The walker, 2026-10-13: 'If we change the door widths, that's ok, it should be called out in the agent contract' -- and, asked which way, 'widen the doors and keep 1.25'. Before 0.214.0 the library built 200 walkable doors under 1.25 in 32 of 132 enterable buildings -- 13 at 1.0 m, 74 at 1.1, 113 at 1.2, 47 of those width-less and so at the builder's own default, then 1.2 -- and the presets wrote 61 more at 1.1 and 1.2. None was under the bake's 1.00 (see derivation), and the library's shells all passed the nav gate. Since 0.214.0 a width-less door resolves to this, every preset writes its doors at it, the staff door asks for it, and migrate_door_width.py widened the library's 152 authored doors about their own centres, one slid along its wall clear of a partition's end (final_stand's west_entry). TWO DOORS STAY UNDER IT, named so they are not read as oversights. primos_pizza's kitchen_stairs stays 1.20 m: between a partition's end (layout_lint L18) and the basement stair's hole (L21) no place on that wall holds 1.25, so it widens when the stair moves (migrate_door_width.KEPT). The landing doors stairs-first generation punches are the corridor's width, min_corridor_width_m, 1.1 m today (stair_core._PUNCH_DOOR_W): every crossing one is punched in measured 1.1 to 1.2 m, so at 1.25 none of the 20 in stair_regression's 140 variants is punched and its checks fail 21 times against 2; Level Factory never builds stairs-first. An Empty's doors are shut and nothing walks through them, so they keep theirs. Held by test_door_width.py; validate.py's navigability check only warns on a door under this.
clearances.re_derive_when: characters.player.radius_m moves -- and with it nav_bake.agent_radius_m, the fattest body plus 0.05 -- or nav_bake.cell_size_m moves. Re-derive min_corridor_width_m (2*agent_radius + 0.3) and the bake's door floor in derivation. min_door_width_m must stay at or over that floor, and test_door_width.py fails until the derivation's figure and the floor agree; it is a design number, so choose what it becomes rather than letting it fall to the floor -- it gives a body (min_door_width - 2*radius)/2 a side, 0.275 m at the ratified body. No door in Deli Counter's code needs editing after that: presets.DOOR_W, the width-less default, the staff door and the staff aisle, the stair landing's opening, presets.STAIR_FLIGHT_WIDTH (the corridor plus a cell) and stair_core's punched landing door all read this block. The library's specs carry written widths: run migrate_door_width.py, which widens every authored door under the minimum it reads here, and layout_lint names any that no longer fit. The stair landing (stairwell.LANDING_DEPTH, with presets.STAIR_FLIGHT_WIDTH) and the vault's opening (vault_room.APERTURE, spec_types' vault default) follow too since 0.215.0: stair_landing_derivation, vault_aperture_derivation. WRITTEN, NOT FOLLOWING: the library's vault rooms carry their opening as written numbers (three, 1.3 x 2.1, written by vault_room when each room was built), and no migration rewrites them yet; the library's doors are re-widened by migrate_door_width.py as above. Then rebuild every shell and re-run the gates (the factory's docs/AGENT_CONTRACT.md).
clearances.stair_landing_derivation: A stair's landing is as deep as the flight Deli Counter draws is wide: agent_contract.stair_flight_width(), min_corridor_width_m plus one nav_bake.cell_size_m, 1.2 m at this contract -- presets.STAIR_FLIGHT_WIDTH and stairwell.LANDING_DEPTH both read it (0.215.0; LANDING_DEPTH was a literal 1.2 recorded as a game-readability default, the same number). The rule is the building code's: IBC 2018 section 1011.6 gives a landing a depth, measured in the direction of travel, of the stairway's width or 48 in (1.219 m), whichever is less. The 48 in cap is left out on purpose: it assumes a human body, and this contract sets the body, so a wider character gets a wider flight and a deeper landing together. A library stair drawn at another width keeps the generator's landing; the code's rule per stair (its own width) would move every narrower library stair's reservation, and is not taken.
clearances.vault_aperture_derivation: The round vault door's opening is min_door_width_m rounded up to the next 0.1 m by min_headroom_m plus 0.1, on the floor: 1.3 x 2.1 m, sill 0, at this contract (agent_contract.vault_aperture(); vault_room.APERTURE and spec_types' vault default read it since 0.215.0 -- both were literals with a comment giving this rule). The sill is 0 because 0.15 put a step above unassisted_step_max_m in the doorway. Deli Counter writes the opening into the vault door's slot (fit.openings) and Zoo builds the door to it; Zoo's vault_forms.DEFAULT_OPENING serves only a standalone build that describes no opening.
clearances.unassisted_step_derivation: A capsule meets a low step on its bottom HEMISPHERE, so the contact normal is sloped rather than horizontal: normal.y = (R - h) / R. The engine calls that contact a floor only while its angle stays inside floor_max_angle, so the tallest step a body WALKS up with no step-up code is R * (1 - cos(floor_max_angle)) = 0.35 * (1 - cos 45 deg) = 0.1025. R is characters.player.radius_m -- the BODY. It is not nav_bake.agent_radius_m, which this field previously used: that one is deliberately larger than any body ('fattest navigating character + 0.05 safety', see nav_bake.note) and using it recorded 0.117 while the gate enforcing it reported 0.103, two numbers for one quantity. characters.player.max_step_up_m (0.5) is what a controller can LIFT itself over; this is what it can walk over with none. The deliverable ships into projects with none of this toolchain present, so a transition above this line requires the consumer to have implemented step-up themselves.

sightlines.aim_height_is: characters.player.chest_height_m. Carried here as well because this block is read as a unit -- the crossing height below needs all three numbers in one place -- but the body is where it is decided, and agent_contract.chest_height() reads the body and checks it against that body's capsule.
sightlines.derivation: A sightline is TWO lines, not one: each side sights from its own eye at the other's chest, so one descends while the other climbs and a solid tall enough to break one can sit under the other. Half a broken sightline is not half a fix -- either side seeing the other is a shot, and the clock starts on the first shot by EITHER side. The shortest solid that breaks both is where the two lines cross: with sight heights a and b and a shared aim height c, h = a - (a - c)^2 / (a + b - 2c) = 1.6 - 0.36 / 1.2 = 1.3. When both sides sight from the same height this reduces to (a + c) / 2, which is what lot/site_cover.MIN_COVER_HEIGHT derives from its copies of the heights, held to Laser Tag's by Level Factory's lasertag_contract.check_sight_drift, and what Level Factory's sightline advisory derives from the body each run fields (Level Factory 0.230.0, the factory's roadmap 289). Nothing in the factory carries the old 1.2 any more, the crossing of the crew's 1.4 sight height before Laser Tag 0.20.0 (searched 2026-10-21: no assignment of a 1.4 eye or a 1.2 crossing in any tool's code). BELOW THIS HEIGHT A SOLID IS SCENERY, NOT COVER: one side keeps a free shot and nothing about the engagement changed.
sightlines.measured_from: Laser Tag 0.20.0, read 2026-09-10. ONE FIELD PER BODY, and the harness places the nodes: LT_TestScenario carries player_eye_height_m 1.6, enemy_eye_height_m 1.6 and aim_height_m 1.0, and LT_MapEvalHarness positions the crew camera, the enemy Marker3D_Eye and BOTH muzzles from them. Before 0.20.0 the numbers that decided this were 1.4 (a literal inside LT_BotPlayerController), 1.5 (LT_EnemyPill.tscn) and 1.0 (a const), and they crossed at 1.2222
sightlines.resolved: Roadmap 131, Laser Tag 0.20.0. SEVEN heights described one firefight and no two agreed: the crew saw from 1.4 and shot from 1.55, the enemy saw from 1.5 and shot from 1.3, LT_PlayerRegistry targeted from 1.4 again, LT_MapSampler measured the map from its own 1.5, and the crew camera alone followed this contract. A body could decline a shot its own barrel had, and the forward offsets could put that barrel through the wall it was standing behind. A body's eye is now a NODE, LT_LineOfSightTester.eye_position is the only way to ask where it is, and each muzzle sits at its own eye -- so the firing ray is the ray the visibility test just proved clear. The crossing moved 1.2222 -> 1.3 and flags the same 39 of 91 combat rooms, because the shipped corpus has nothing between 1.20 m and 1.40 m
sightlines.re_derive_when: any of the four heights above moves, or a controller learns to crouch. Nothing in this toolchain crouches -- characters.player.crouch_height_m has no consumer in Laser Tag or Lot -- so a solid below this height is life rather than shelter, and that is a statement about the evaluator, not about the shipped game.
